title: Shepherd of Tender Youth
description: Shepherd of Tender Youth in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 5 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Clement of Alexandria. The English translation is by Henry Martyn Dexter (1846). The tune, ITALIAN HYMN, is by Felice de Giardini (1769). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: Shep-herd of ten_-der youth, Gui-ding in love__ and truth, Through de-vious ways! Christ, our tri-um-phant King! We come your Name to sing, And here our chil-dren bring, To shout your praise.

lines: We come your Name to sing,
You might now save our race,
You are our soul's High Priest!
None calls on you in vain,
Lead us where you have trod,
So now, and till we die,

topics: Children (see also God's Children - the Faithful)
licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
credits: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (openhymnal.org), edited by Brian J. Dumont; public domain.
reviewNotes: Held back: the score gives no year for the words; not provably public domain: "textPublished" must be a year before 1929.
